column2: Evil grumbling, divine hearing and anger precede fire consuming a part of the camp. The extent is not expanded to its outskirts or the whole camp.
The people cry to Moses, Moses prays to the Lord, and the fire subsides. The chain of agents remains.
Burning translates the selected Greek place-name and its fire explanation rather than substituting another-language name.
The mixed company craves intensely; Israel's sons also sit and weep. The source's sitting action is retained without adding again.
Free fish and all five named vegetables are preserved. The remembered claim belongs to the speakers.
Parched life represents the soul idiom, followed by eyes fixed on nothing but manna. The sensory and lack expressions both remain.
Coriander seed and crystal are the selected comparisons. Crystal is not replaced by a substance from a different source tradition.
Gathering, grinding, crushing, boiling and ash-baked cakes remain distinct preparations, followed by an oil-cake taste comparison.
column3: The precise culinary equivalents for the two cake terms need lexical review; current wording remains provisional.

column2: Night dew descends on camp and manna descends upon it; the antecedent remains the dew.
Moses hears weeping by groups at doorways. The Lord's great anger and Moses' adverse reaction are separately stated.
Moses addresses God with Thou forms and asks about affliction and favour. Onrush retains the selected pressure imagery rather than silently substituting the later burden noun.
column3: Onrush is difficult spoken English; a fuller lexical and spoken-stage decision remains open.

column2: Conceiving and giving birth are negative rhetorical questions; the nurse image and promised land remain. Your inside the quotation addresses Moses, while Thou outside addresses God.
Moses asks where to obtain meat for all and quotes the people's demand. No supply is implied to exist already.
Alone and too heavy explain Moses' inability. The future inability and this matter expression remain.
The literary proposal uses dost for the present direct address to God, smoothing the inherited if Thou do construction while retaining the conditional request, emphatic killing and mercy clause.
Seventy known elders and scribes are gathered to stand with Moses at the tent. The number and both roles remain.
God descends, speaks, takes of the Spirit upon Moses and places it on them; shared bearing answers his inability to bear alone.
Purification is for tomorrow; the repeated meat promise and quoted claim about Egypt remain, including the source's present is well.
The escalating exclusions retain all five durations: one, two, five, ten and twenty days.
A month, nostrils and sickness retain the selected bodily imagery. Disobedience to the Lord among them and the Egypt question explain it.
column3: Bilious sickness is provisional for the ancient disease term; it is not an asserted modern diagnosis.

column2: Moses names 600,000 on foot and repeats the month-long meat promise. Thou addresses God; the embedded I is God's promise.
The two sufficiency questions concern slaughtered livestock and the sea's food. All qualifies the latter.
column3: The breadth of the first livestock term and its conventional sheep rendering need consistency review with other flock passages.

column2: The Lord's hand and the overtaking word answer the sufficiency objection. The question expects divine sufficiency rather than denying it.
Moses reports the divine words and stations seventy elders around the tent.
The Lord comes in cloud, distributes from the Spirit upon Moses, and the elders prophesy. Did not do so again follows the selected negative continuation clause.
Two enrolled men remain in camp and receive the Spirit despite not going to the tent. The conventional Medad equivalent for Greek Modad remains provisional.
The young man's report names both prophets and locates them in the camp; it does not add an accusation.
Joshua is the chosen attendant in the selected wording, not one serving from youth. My lord addresses Moses with ordinary human-address grammar.
Moses questions jealousy on his behalf and wishes all the Lord's people prophets, connected to the gift of the Spirit. The universal scope remains.
Moses and Israel's elders go back into camp; both parties are explicit.
Wind from the Lord brings the birds from the sea, with a day's distance on each side and about two cubits from the ground.
column3: Quail is retained provisionally for the bird term; the spatial description is not converted into a measured layer of piled birds.

column2: All day, all night and the following day remain; the least collection is ten kors. The repeated cooling language is represented provisionally.
column3: Cooled them in cooling places is awkward and needs fuller lexical and spoken-stage work; no unverified drying process is asserted.

column2: Meat still in the teeth and not yet gone precedes the severe divine plague. The text does not specify unchewed meat.
Graves of Craving translates the selected place-name and preserves the burial explanation.
Departure from Graves of Craving to Hazeroth is followed by the repeated statement of being there.
Miriam precedes Aaron in the complaint; Ethiopian woman and Moses' marrying her are repeated as in the selected text. No identity with another named wife is supplied.
The two questions contrast Moses alone with the speakers also; divine hearing closes the complaint.
Moses' meekness is compared with all people on earth. The statement's universal comparison is retained.
Immediate summons names Moses, Miriam and Aaron and repeats all three coming to the tent.
The Lord descends in a cloud pillar and stands at the entrance; Aaron and Miriam are called and both come forward.
The conditional prophet receives divine self-disclosure in vision and speech in sleep. The unusual unto the Lord phrase remains.
column3: The compact prophet-among-you-unto-the-Lord construction needs further syntactic review.

column2: Moses differs as the servant faithful in the whole house. The negative contrast and all are retained.
Mouth-to-mouth speech, visible appearance and no riddles distinguish Moses; he saw the Lord's glory in the selected past tense. The accusation ends as a question.
Fierce anger is directed at both complainants; the Lord departs. No new recipient of punishment is added here.
The cloud withdraws and Miriam is leprous like snow; Aaron's look and the repeated discovery remain.
Aaron beseeches Moses using you, admits ignorance and sin, and asks that sin not be laid on them.
The death and miscarried-child images retain the selected active consumes and feminine her rather than replacing them with a familiar passive description.
column3: The consuming subject and feminine referent are difficult and require syntactic and apparatus review.

column2: Moses' brief healing petition addresses God with Thee and keeps the woman as its object.
The father's spitting analogy expects seven days of shame. Seven days outside camp and subsequent re-entry are retained.
Miriam's exclusion lasts seven days; Israel waits until she is cleansed, following the selected wording rather than merely gathered in.
Afterward the people leave Hazeroth and camp in Paran; the sequence remains.
